a.agency_actions: Document access control decisions that are specific to this information system
a.fedramp_guidance: Some policies and procedures will be inherited from other agency systems and/or cloud systems. You do not need to repeat that information here.

b.fedramp_guidance: Determine the agency role or personnel accountable for the policies and procedures in this control family. This is an agency position and should not be assigned to the cloud service provider. This person or role may not be responsible for all implementation, monitoring, or enforcement of the controls but should be accountable to leadership for compliance with all relevant policies and procedures.

c.fedramp_guidance: How often and by whom will the policies and procedures in this control family be reviewed? Provide a broad policy here (e.g. “Policies and procedures will be reviewed at least annually or in response to any relevant incidents or changes”) and then provide more detailed additional review requirements for specific controls as needed.

a.agency_actions: Define authorized use case(s), and identify the account types (individual, shared/group, service, guest, emergency, temporary, etc.) the system will and won't use.
a.fedramp_guidance: What specific business functions, processes, programs, users and missions will the information system support? This should be an exhaustive list and any additional use cases not specified should require approval form the AO and trigger a review of the Authorization. Explicitly prohibit any account type not needed for the defined use cases (e.g., prohibit guest/anonymous accounts if not required).

b.fedramp_guidance: The ACO should be assigned the root/admin account and be responsible for granting access to other individuals within the agency. The ACO may grant access directly in the information system/cloud service or through assignment of roles/groups in an Agency IdP used for single sign on.

c.agency_actions: Determine requirements (training, role, etc) that are required for access
c.fedramp_guidance: The agency is responsible for training agency users and determining other criteria for access (clearance level, job function, etc). The CSP is separately and solely responsible for training and role assignment of its own staff. Review the CSP’s training and other related processes to ensure you are satisfied.

d.agency_actions: Identify users, roles/groups and permissions for the information system
d.fedramp_guidance: Define all users of the system. Agencies should define roles or groups of users rather than individual users. For each defined role, identify the permissions that are required.

e.agency_actions: Define the approval process for access
e.fedramp_guidance: Explicitly define the approval process before a user is given access to the cloud service. Is access automatically granted to users with certain roles or in certain groups? Must access be approved by a supervisor? Are there any per user costs and if so how will the agency verify availability of funds?

f.fedramp_guidance: Identify specific agency procedures to create, enable, modify, disable, and remove accounts. Review the provider's Secure Configuration Guidance to ensure that the provider's account management procedures are consistent with agency procedures.

g.fedramp_guidance: The agency is responsible only for monitoring and reporting activity by agency users.  The CSP is separately and solely responsible for monitoring and reporting activity by its own staff and other users of the system.

h.agency_actions: Notify account managers within a defined time period when an account is no longer required, a user is terminated or transferred, or usage/need-to-know changes.
h.fedramp_guidance: This is a distinct notification duty, not the disable action itself — that's covered in AC-02 (03). Define the maximum time between the triggering event and notification, and identify who must be notified (e.g., the ACO from part b).

i.agency_actions: Define the basis on which access is authorized.
i.fedramp_guidance: Access to the information system should require a valid approval defined in part e, a valid usage requirement defined in part a, and compliance with all agency requiements defined in part c.

j.agency_actions: Define the account review frequency and who performs it.
j.fedramp_guidance: Determine the frequency or triggers that will require an account review, and prefer a recurring automated report over a manual audit. Where the agency IdP is the source of truth, this review is a reconciliation: accounts present in the cloud service but not in the IdP are the finding.

k.fedramp_guidance: Best Practice: Avoid the use of shared or group accounts. Role based access controls should make it simple enough to allow each user to maintain an individual account for authentication and auditing purposes while still sharing responsibility and authorization across a team. If shared accounts must be used, determine a safe process to rotate authenticators when access to the shared account changes. Consider the use of tools that can store shared authenticators safely so that authorized users can provide the shared token for authentication without knowing the actual value.

l.agency_actions: Align account management with agency personnel termination and transfer processes.
l.fedramp_guidance: Ensure that agency termination and transfer processes will revoke the user's access to the information system.
l.notes: This is normally inherited from the agency's existing joiner-mover-leaver process; the requirement is that the cloud service is included in it. Confirm that a termination or transfer recorded in the agency HR system results in the account being disabled in the service, whether through IdP deprovisioning or an explicit step. Services reached directly rather than through single sign-on are the common failure here.

_.agency_actions: Define the automated mechanisms that will be used to apply, monitor, and manage system accounts
_.fedramp_guidance: For Moderate or High information systems the process of managing the account life cycle must be automated. This is typically delivered through the CSP's account-provisioning API or SCIM integration with the agency IdP, per the Secure Configuration Guide, rather than agency-built tooling.

_.agency_actions: Configure automatic expiry/removal for temporary and emergency accounts, and document the approval, monitoring, and audit process around them.
_.fedramp_guidance: Best Practice: Avoid utilizing temporary accounts entirely. Rather, focus on streamlining standard account management workflows so they are efficient enough to accommodate urgent or short-term needs. In cases where temporary accounts are unavoidable, clearly specify and document the exact personnel authorized to approve them. You must also implement continuous monitoring to maintain an accurate inventory of temporary accounts at all times, supported by a periodic audit process to ensure any unneeded access is promptly revoked. These same governance protocols should also apply to temporary role assignments or elevated permissions that an individual does not typically require.

_.agency_actions: Document process for disabling accounts that have expired, are no longer associated with a user, are in violation of agency policy, or are not in use and are no longer required.
_.fedramp_guidance: For Moderate or High information systems determine the permitted time period before expired, inactive, or otherwise anomalous accounts must be disabled.
_.notes: Check with the provider for the best way to identify inactive accounts and disable or remove them.

_.agency_actions: Automatically audit account actions
_.fedramp_guidance: For Moderate or High information systems auditing should be automated to ensure that account actions are monitored and any deviations from expected permissions are identified and addressed promptly.

_.agency_actions: Document your inactivity logout policy
_.fedramp_guidance: If the service is accessible only from GFE then this control is likely already met by inactivity timeouts built into the GFE. For services that can be accessed on non-GFE work with the provider to implement inactivity timeout.
_.notes: The agency SSP should document only the agency’s role in implementing a control. For example, the technical details of how inactivity is monitored and how sessions are terminated is likely being handled by the CSP. The agency should only need to document configuration settings they set to enable the inactivity logout.

_.agency_actions: Manage privileged user accounts
_.fedramp_guidance: Privileged user accounts in this context are accounts assigned to agency staff that perform certain security-relevant functions that ordinary users are not authorized to perform. Privileged roles include key management, account management, and web administration. Establish these accounts under a role- or attribute-based scheme, monitor assignments and changes to them, and revoke access when an individual's role no longer justifies it. The CSP maintains its own parallel privileged-account program, evidenced through the Certification Package rather than something the agency manages.

_.agency_actions: Document the process for shared and group account management including approvals, monitoring, and auditing.
_.fedramp_guidance: Shared or group accounts inroduce increased risk due to the lack of accountability with such accounts. Agencies should define strict policies for the creation of such accounts, how credentials are managed and shared, and how usage of the sahred account is mmonitored. Shared accounts are distinct from service accounts which are intended to be used by automated processes.
_.notes: Best Practice: Avoid the use of shared or group accounts. Role based access controls should make it simple enough to allow each user to maintain an individual account for authentication and auditing purposes while still sharing responsibility and authorization across a team. If it is necessary to use shared accounts be sure that your process can still capture attribution for any actions taken by the shared account.

_.agency_actions: Monitor and report atypical usage of system accounts
_.fedramp_guidance: The agency must maintain an inventory of system accounts created and used by the agency and must monitor these accounts for atypical usage. Instances of atypical usage should be investigated as incidents until determined otherwise. This covers agency-managed accounts only — the CSP separately monitors and reports atypical usage by its own staff.

_.agency_actions: Disable accounts of individuals determined to be of high risk for misuse.
_.fedramp_guidance: Integrate account management with related agency personnel management processes. Close coordination among system administrators, legal staff, human resource managers, and authorizing officials is essential when disabling system accounts for high-risk individuals. This applies to agency staff — the CSP has its own separate process for disabling its own staff's access for the same reason.

_.agency_actions: Review Cloud Service documentation
_.fedramp_guidance: Once roles and privileges are assigned, enforcement is handled by the Cloud Service. Review relevant cloud service documentation to ensure you are satisfied.

_.agency_actions: Document and enforce information flow control policy for agency data flows
_.fedramp_guidance: Data flows within the cloud service and between the cloud service and other non-agency systems will be enforced by the provider. The agency is responsible for data flows between agency information systems and the cloud service provider. The agency defines an information flow control policy governing data into/out of the CSO (data types, classification, direction).
_.notes: Examples: The Agency SIEM will receive telemetry data from the cloud service by accessing an API authenticated using an API key which will be rotated every 30 days. Agency general counsel will be able to access a compliance API to respond to FOIA requests using individual accounts granted to each authorized member of the GC team.

_.agency_actions: Review Certification Package. Identify the information flows that must be kept separate.
_.fedramp_guidance: Separation of information flows inside the cloud service is implemented by the CSP. The agency determines which of its own flows require separation — by mission, by data type, or by community of interest — and whether the service's tenancy, workspace, or project boundaries can express that separation. This is closely related to SC-04; where the tenancy model is documented there, reference that entry rather than repeating it.
_.notes: This control enhancement is not part of the standard NIST Moderate baseline but is added by FedRAMP. This control is particularly important for cloud services operated by commercial vendors.

a.agency_actions: Determine which system roles must be mutually exclusive to ensure proper oversight
a.fedramp_guidance: The most common issue is the chain of approval for assigning roles and permissions. In general, the ACO and other user roles that can grant elevated access should not be a business user of the system.

b.agency_actions: Enforce separation of duty access restrictions
b.fedramp_guidance: Best option: The separation of duties is enforced by the cloud service itself. No agency action required. Second best option: The agency enforces these restrictions through their own IdP system which automatically manages roles within the cloud service. If neither option is feasible the agency should define and document an enforcement mechanism including an audit and monitoring plan.

_.agency_actions: Use Least Privilege principles when assigning authorizations
_.fedramp_guidance: Grant the minimum authorizations needed for each role's assigned tasks and re-evaluate them when roles change. Where the cloud service offers coarse roles only — for example a single administrator role bundling unrelated privileges — document the gap and compensate with monitoring rather than assuming the role is acceptable. This is closely tied to AC-02 d; where roles and permissions are documented there, reference that entry rather than repeating it.

_.agency_actions: Determine which agency individuals/roles are authorized to access the security functions and security-relevant information exposed to the agency within the system.
_.fedramp_guidance: Security functions include establishing system accounts, configuring access authorizations, configuring audited events, and intrusion detection parameters; security-relevant information includes firewall/router filtering rules, security service configuration, cryptographic key management, and access control lists. For Rev5 packages, FedRAMP assigns the CSP's own scope for this control as all such functions and information not publicly accessible (ac-06.01_odp.02/.05) — expect the CSP's control response to reflect that comprehensive scope, but this doesn't dictate the agency's own determination. Consult the CSP's Secure Configuration Guidance to see what security functions and information are exposed to the agency's tenant, then decide which agency individuals/roles need access to them.

_.agency_actions: For any agency individual/role authorized under AC-06 (01) to access security functions or security-relevant information, require they use a separate, non-privileged account for routine non-security tasks.
_.fedramp_guidance: This overlaps with AC-06 (01) — reference that entry for the CSP-side scope and available functions rather than repeating it here. Most ordinary agency users have no access to these functions and are unaffected by this control; it applies only to agency staff who hold elevated access.

_.agency_actions: Designate a specific, limited set of agency personnel or roles authorized to hold privileged accounts for the system; do not grant privileged access broadly.
_.fedramp_guidance: Restricting privileged accounts to a defined set of personnel or roles limits how many accounts could expose privileged functions or information if compromised or misused. This is closely tied to least privilege and separation of duties — reference AC-06 and AC-05 for the underlying role/permission model rather than repeating it here. The CSP separately restricts privileged accounts among its own staff.

_.agency_actions: Define the frequency and scope (roles or classes of users) for reviewing currently assigned privileges, and reassign or remove any that are no longer justified by mission/business need.
_.fedramp_guidance: This is a privilege-level counterpart to the account review in AC-02 j — that review asks whether an account should still exist, this one asks whether its current privileges are still justified. Prefer a recurring automated report of privilege assignments by role over a manual audit where the cloud service or agency IdP can generate one.

_.agency_actions: Validate privileged functions are logged by the cloud service
_.fedramp_guidance: Review the cloud service logging to ensure that privileged functions are captured in sufficient detail and that these logs are available to the agency.

_.agency_actions: Review Cloud Service documentation
_.fedramp_guidance: Once roles and privileges are assigned, enforcement is handled by the Cloud Service. Review relevant cloud service documentation to ensure you are satisfied.

a.agency_actions: Determine the number and frequency of invalid login attempts that should trigger an action
a.fedramp_guidance: Consult CSP provided Secure Configuration Guidance to determine what options are available.

b.agency_actions: Configure the desired action when failed login criteria is exceeded
b.fedramp_guidance: Document the agency specific configuration settings applied.  Determine if the enforcement will be implemented by the CSP or by an agency system such as the agency IdP service. Document the service(s) responsible for enforcement.

a.agency_actions: Determine system use notification requirements relevant to the specific information system.
a.fedramp_guidance: Determine if a system use notification is required. If you are using an agency IdP or similar system to control authentication the requirement for a system use notification may already be met. A system specific use notification should still be used if the agency cannot be sure a sufficient use notification will be presented elsewhere in the authentication process or if there is additional relevant information specific to the cloud service that should be presented.

b.agency_actions: Ensure users acknowledge the system use notification.
b.fedramp_guidance: Confirm with the service provider (or agency IdP, if it fronts authentication) that the notification is retained on screen until the user explicitly acknowledges it and takes an affirmative action to proceed — not just displayed.

c.agency_actions: Determine any system use notification requirements for publicly accessible systems or functions and document as needed.
c.fedramp_guidance: For publicly accessible systems or functions that will not follow an authentication workflow, consult the CSP Secure Configuration Guidance for how to configure system use notifications and document the configuration.

a.agency_actions: Review Cloud Service documentation
a.fedramp_guidance: For systems accessible only from GFE, the device lock control should be implemented at the OS level and no additional implementation is required.  For systems accessible from non-GFE or if the GFE lock controls are deemed insufficient for the specific system, determine if a policy control is sufficient or if a technical control is needed. Review CSP Secure Configuration Guide to determine what options are available and if needed discuss specific requirements with the CSP to determine the best approach. Document any specific configurations used to implement this control.

b.fedramp_guidance: For systems accessible only from GFE, the device lock control should be implemented at the OS level and no additional implementation is required — confirm the OS lock requires re-authentication (not just any keystroke) to resume the session. For systems accessible from non-GFE or if the GFE lock controls are deemed insufficient, determine if a policy or technical control is needed, and confirm it likewise requires re-authentication before regaining access. Review CSP Secure Configuration Guide to determine what options are available. Document any specific configurations used.

_.agency_actions: Review Cloud Service documentation
_.fedramp_guidance: For systems accessible only from GFE, the device lock control should be implemented at the OS level and no additional implementation is required — confirm the OS lock screen displays a non-revealing image or pattern rather than simply blanking or leaving prior content visible. For systems accessible from non-GFE or if the GFE lock controls are deemed insufficient, review CSP Secure Configuration Guide to determine what options are available. Document any specific configurations used.

_.agency_actions: Determine scenarios in which sessions with the cloud service(S) should be terminated.
_.fedramp_guidance: The agency must determine what conditions or events will trigger a termination. Then review Secure Configuration Guidance to implement the control. Document any specific configurations used to implement this control. Sessions can be terminated at multiple points in the authorization/workflow chain. For example, session termination within the agency IdP may or may not terminate open sessions with the cloud service.

a.agency_actions: Review Cloud Service documentation
a.fedramp_guidance: Specific user actions such as authentication or accessing support information may be inherently accessible to unauthenticated users. In other cases certain functions require unauthenticated access to achieve specific business functions such as hosting a publicly available website.  Review the cloud service documentation to determine what functionality/information is available to unauthenticated users and ensure this aligns with your agency’s requirements for both functionality and security.  Document any specific configurations used to implement this control.

b.fedramp_guidance: Specify the business use case for any system operations permitted without prior user identification.

a.agency_actions: Identify remote access types. Establish policies for all remote access types.
a.fedramp_guidance: Take advantage of conditional access, device compliance checks, session timeouts, and location/risk-based restriction features built into the SaaS product, which are typically outlined within each cloud service’s Secure Configuration Guidance. Regularly audit and update your Agency’s remote access control policies as it relates to the cloud service. Develop additional criteria for reassessing remote access policies, for example: after your Agency experiences an incident/breach, after a change to the cloud service occurs (see FR SCN process), etc…
a.notes: Most of the NIST AC-17 Supplemental Guidance discusses VPNs. However SaaS services are typically NOT accessed using VPN connections. Agency access to SaaS services is inherently remote.

b.fedramp_guidance: For a system built on a cloud service, effectively all agency access is remote access. Authorize each distinct access path before it is used — browser, API and CLI clients, mobile applications, and any machine-to-machine integration — and record the authorization alongside the use cases defined in AC-02 a. Block paths the agency has not authorized where the service supports doing so.

_.agency_actions: Monitor and enforce remote access policies using automation.
_.fedramp_guidance: Monitoring of remote access to the service is implemented by the CSP; the agency's part is ensuring the resulting records reach agency monitoring. Review the Secure Configuration Guide for the log feeds and administrative event streams the service exposes, and connect them to the agency SIEM rather than reviewing them in the provider's console.

_.agency_actions: Configure encryption for your cloud tenant
_.fedramp_guidance: Configure the SaaS product to only accept encrypted connections. This is typically outlined within each cloud service’s Secure Configuration Guidance. This overlaps with SC-08 — see that entry for the general encryption-in-transit treatment; this row is the remote-access-specific instance of the same requirement.

_.agency_actions: Limit remote access to managed access points.
_.fedramp_guidance: Usually this is accomplished by restricting access to Agency-managed GFE. On the provider side, the CSP's own network segmentation and ingress controls are evidenced under the Cloud Native Architecture Key Security Indicators for 20x providers; the agency's own action is limited to restricting access to agency-managed GFE.

_.agency_actions: Generate a audit trail for privileged and security-related commands/actions.
_.fedramp_guidance: Determine which privileged actions in the service must produce assessable evidence, and confirm the service records them in a form the agency can retain and review. Part (b) requires the rationale for privileged remote access to be documented in the agency SSP.

a.agency_actions: Define and document mobile device usage and configuration policies.
a.fedramp_guidance: Focus on device management policies for accessing the cloud service. Utilize your Agency IdP to enforce device compliance (e.g., ensuring devices are company-issued or MDM-enrolled) before allowing access to the cloud tenant. Review CSP documentation for supported mobile configurations and security features.

b.agency_actions: Establish a process to authorize and register mobile devices for system access.
b.fedramp_guidance: Implement authorization workflows that require devices to meet security criteria (e.g., OS version, security patches) prior to enabling access to the cloud service.

_.agency_actions: Review the CSP's cryptographic-module documentation to confirm what encryption is used on mobile access paths.
_.fedramp_guidance: Review the CSP's Secure Configuration Guide and cryptographic-module documentation (required under CMU-CSO-CMD) to confirm what encryption is used on mobile access paths. CMVP validation is a SHOULD, not a MUST, at Class C — a documented-but-unvalidated module is not itself a finding.

a.agency_actions: Define and document policies for access initiated from an external system
a.fedramp_guidance: This control specifically addresses access to the agency information system by an external system. This is likely not the case for the Cloud Service(s) the information system is using. Examples of external systems covered by this control would include personally owned systems, other agency information systems, or other commercial cloud services. External systems used to access public interfaces to organizational systems are outside the scope of AC-20

b.agency_actions: Define and document prohibited types of external systems
b.fedramp_guidance: Define specific types of systems that are universally banned. For example you might want to prohibit the use of personal devices or ban access from any system operated while in certain countries.

_.agency_actions: Define the verification-or-agreement basis for permitting external-system use.
_.fedramp_guidance: Before permitting an external system (per AC-20 a/b) to access this system or its data, either verify the external system implements the controls required by agency policy, or retain an approved system connection/processing agreement — FedRAMP's guidance for AC-20 ties this agreement to CA-3.

_.agency_actions: Define restrictions on the use of organization-controlled portable storage devices by authorized individuals on external systems
_.fedramp_guidance: This control describes the scenario where an authorized user connected a portable storage device containing organization controlled information to an external system. This should generally not be necessary.

a.agency_actions: Confirm the cloud service can show a user's effective access to a specific item, not just the individual grants that make it up.
a.fedramp_guidance: Layered permission models make it hard to determine a user's actual access by inspecting individual grants alone — for example, a user might be explicitly granted read access, inherit write access through one group, and be explicitly restricted through another group, with the platform resolving which wins. Confirm the cloud service provides an equivalent tool to compute and display a user's final effective access to a given item (per the Secure Configuration Guide) before authorized users are expected to judge whether a sharing partner's access matches the information's restrictions.

b.agency_actions: Employ tooling or a manual process that helps users decide whether to share information with a specific partner.
b.fedramp_guidance: Review whether the cloud service offers information-labeling, classification, data-loss-prevention, or effective-access-calculation features (see AC-21 a) that help users judge whether a sharing partner's access matches the information's restrictions. Where the service offers no such tooling, define a manual review process for the circumstances the agency has identified as requiring discretion.

a.agency_actions: Designate individuals authorized to make information publicly accessible
a.fedramp_guidance: This control applies only where the agency information system publishes content to the public. Where it does, tie the designation to a role rather than to named individuals so it survives staff changes. Where the system has no publicly accessible component, record that determination rather than leaving the control unaddressed.

b.agency_actions: Train authorized individuals to ensure that publicly accessible information does not contain nonpublic information
b.fedramp_guidance: Training for this population is normally inherited from existing agency records management and public affairs training. Reference the agency system that provides it rather than building a separate course for this information system.

c.agency_actions: Review the proposed content of information prior to posting onto the publicly accessible system to ensure that nonpublic information is not included
c.fedramp_guidance: Define who performs the pre-publication review and what they check for — personally identifiable information, procurement-sensitive material, and internal system detail are the usual findings. This is an agency process; the cloud service will not perform it.

d.agency_actions: Review the content on the publicly accessible system for nonpublic information and remove such information, if discovered
d.fedramp_guidance: Determine the frequency with which reviews will occur

a.agency_actions: Develop, and document awareness and training policy
a.fedramp_guidance: Some policies and procedures will be inherited from other agency systems and/or cloud systems. You do not need to repeat that information here.

b.fedramp_guidance: Determine the agency role or personnel accountable for the policies and procedures. This person or role may not be responsible for all implementation, monitoring, or enforcement of the controls but should be accountable to leadership for compliance with all relevant policies and procedures.

c.agency_actions: Review and update the awareness and training
c.fedramp_guidance: Define the frequency and designate responsible parties for reviewing policies and procedures. For instance: “Policies and procedures will be reviewed at least annually or following relevant incidents or changes”. Include detailed review requirements for specific controls as appropriate.

a.agency_actions: Provide security and privacy literacy training to users of this system as part of initial onboarding, periodically thereafter, and when required by system changes.
a.fedramp_guidance: Typically inherited from the agency's existing enterprise security-awareness training program (see AT-01). Where the CSP provides service-specific usage or security training material, that can supplement but does not replace the agency's own training. KSI-CED-RAT evidences the CSP's own internal staff training, a separate supply-chain data point, not a substitute for this control.

b.agency_actions: Employ specific awareness techniques to increase security and privacy awareness among users of this system.
b.fedramp_guidance: Incorporate hands-on exercises into security and privacy training that mirror real-life scenarios, like social engineering ploys, unauthorized access attempts, or the danger of malicious emails and phishing links.

c.agency_actions: Update literacy training and awareness content on a defined frequency and following defined events.
c.fedramp_guidance: Verify training courses are current and updated, typically as part of the agency's existing training-content review cycle.

d.agency_actions: Incorporate lessons learned from internal or external security incidents or breaches into literacy training and awareness content.
d.fedramp_guidance: Review recent agency and sector incidents for lessons that should be reflected in the next training update — distinct from the periodic content refresh in part c.

_.agency_actions: Provide insider-threat recognition/reporting training to users of this system.
_.fedramp_guidance: Typically inherited from the agency's existing insider-threat training program.

_.agency_actions: Provide social-engineering and social-mining recognition/reporting training to users of this system.
_.fedramp_guidance: Typically inherited from the agency's existing security-awareness training program.

a.agency_actions: Provide role-based security and privacy training to agency personnel with defined roles/responsibilities for this system (e.g., privileged users, administrators), before authorizing access or duties and periodically thereafter.
a.fedramp_guidance: Typically inherited from the agency's existing role-based training program for that role.

b.agency_actions: Update role-based training content on a defined frequency and following defined events.
b.fedramp_guidance: Verify role-specific training is kept current, typically as part of the agency's existing training-content review cycle.

c.agency_actions: Incorporate lessons learned from internal or external security incidents or breaches into role-based training.
c.fedramp_guidance: Review recent agency and sector incidents for role-specific lessons that should be reflected in the next training update.

a.agency_actions: Document and monitor security and privacy training activities for agency personnel who use this system, including both awareness and role-based training.
a.fedramp_guidance: Typically inherited from the agency's existing training-records system (e.g., its LMS). This is a record of the agency's own personnel, not the CSP's.

b.agency_actions: Retain individual training records for agency personnel for the agency-defined retention period.
b.fedramp_guidance: Typically inherited from the agency's existing training-records retention policy.

a.agency_actions: Document audit control decisions that are specific to this information system
a.fedramp_guidance: Some policies and procedures will be inherited from other agency systems and/or cloud systems. You do not need to repeat that information here.

b.fedramp_guidance: Determine the agency role or personnel accountable for the policies and procedures in this control family. This is an agency position and should not be assigned to the cloud service provider. This person or role may not be responsible for all implementation, monitoring, or enforcement of the controls but should be accountable to leadership for compliance with all relevant policies and procedures.

c.fedramp_guidance: How often and by whom will the policies and procedures in this control family be reviewed? Provide a broad policy here (e.g. “Policies and procedures will be reviewed at least annually or in response to any relevant incidents or changes”) and then provide more detailed additional review requirements for specific controls as needed.

a.agency_actions: Identify the types of events that the system is capable of logging
a.fedramp_guidance: Consult the CSPs secure configuration guidance and their response to KSI-MLA-LET (Logging Event Types).

b.agency_actions: Integrate CSP logging into existing agency logging tools
b.fedramp_guidance: The agency should integrate CSP logging information into existing agency monitoring tools. This includes integration in compliance dashboards reviewed by authorizing officials. Although the agency will not manage the CSP system, they remain responsible for accepting any risk of using the system so must be aware of any changes in risk posture.

c.agency_actions: Select CSP log event types that will be included in agency logging systems
c.fedramp_guidance: Work with the CSP to understand which log events will be relevant to your agency use cases and include only those log events that provide meaningful risk analysis.

d.agency_actions: Document reasons for the selected event types
d.fedramp_guidance: Provide guidance for future users or admins of the system to explain what the selected event types mean in terms of agency risk. For example, 'Sensitive user data is stored in database, alert on failure testing database encryption or access control protocols'

e.agency_actions: Determine the frequency to review selected log event types
e.fedramp_guidance: Logging events should be reviewed persistently but you should also determine a cadence for reviewing the kind of log events you are including. This can be time based and/or event driven. For example, reviewing select log events after any incident to be sure all necessary data was captured.

_.agency_actions: Verify log events contain all required data elements
_.fedramp_guidance: Consult the CSP to map data elements in log events to the required information

_.agency_actions: Document any additional information your agency requires in log events
_.fedramp_guidance: Consult the CSP to map data elements in log events to the required information

_.agency_actions: Determine audit log storage capacity
_.fedramp_guidance: Determine what log data must be maintained within agency controlled systems. Consider the log retention provided by the CSP as part of this equation. For example, if a CSP maintains logs indefinitely and the agency is satisfied with the controls protecting those logs you may only need to store current logging information locally and rely on the CSP to provide older logs if needed. Conversely, if the CSP logging retention does not meet statutory requirements the agency should configure their systems to download and retain logs to meet these requirements.

a.agency_actions: Define alerts for logging process failures
a.fedramp_guidance: There are two kinds of failures that should be addressed in this control. The first are failures of the agency logging system. This will likely be inherited from your agency’s SIEM system or other centralized logging capability.  The second is a failure to receive logging information from the CSP. This could include receiving no data for a period of time, connection failures with the CSP logging service, or logs that do not match the expected configuration. Document thresholds for alerting and notification procedures.

b.agency_actions: Determine additional actions required if logging fails
b.fedramp_guidance: Depending on the agency use case, a logging failure may require additional action such as restricting access to the information system or implementing additional manual reporting requirements.

a.agency_actions: Define inappropriate or unusual activity that would be detected in logs
a.fedramp_guidance: Define specific logging events that could indicate inappropriate or unusual activity and should be investigated. Configure alerts to notify personnel or roles defined in AU-06 part b. FedRAMP frames this review/analysis activity as vulnerability detection, governed by the Vulnerability Detection and Response rules (e.g., VDR-CSO-DET) for the CSP's own environment.

b.agency_actions: Define personnel or roles that should be notified in the event of inappropriate or unusual activity
b.fedramp_guidance: Define personnel or roles that will be notified by the agency of inappropriate or unusual activity detected by the agency. This may include both agency and CSP stakeholders.

c.fedramp_guidance: Document procedures for communicating with law enforcement information, intelligence information, or other credible sources of information concerning increased risk to your agency’s use case.
c.notes: This control is generally concerned with how the agency will respond to CUI or classified information that impacts the risk to agency information. In these cases the CSP may not have access to the same information and the agency may need to make adjustments to their own monitoring or other procedures.

_.agency_actions: Automate review, analysis, and reporting of inappropriate or unusual activity
_.fedramp_guidance: Any activity covered by this control should be considered an urgent matter and require immediate investigation. The agency should use automated mechanisms to ensure relevant stakeholders are notified in real time about such events. This automates the same review/analysis activity AU-06 frames as vulnerability detection — see that entry for the applicable FedRAMP rule.

_.agency_actions: Analyze and correlate audit records across different repositories to gain organization-wide situational awareness.
_.fedramp_guidance: The agency may have access to additional logging information such as logs from the agency IdP that allow them to identify inappropriate or unusual activity that could not be detected by the CSP alone.

_.agency_actions: Consider audit record reduction and report generation capability
_.fedramp_guidance: In some cases, the agency may wish to modify raw audit records from the CSP to reduce resource consumption or to make reporting easier. When doing so the agency should consider the CSP provided capacity to retrieve the raw logs in the future

_.agency_actions: Integrate CSP provided log events into agency SIEM or equivalent systems
_.fedramp_guidance: CSP provided log events should be processed using the same agency systems used for agency operated systems when possible.

a.agency_actions: Verify that time stamps on CSP provided logs contain time zone information and can be converted to match other agency logging time stamps
a.fedramp_guidance: Consult the CSP for information about log timestamps

b.agency_actions: Ensure that the granularity of audit records generated by the CSP meet the agency’s requirements.
b.fedramp_guidance: Consult the CSP for information about log timestamps

a.agency_actions: Protect audit information and audit logging tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion
a.fedramp_guidance: This control part applies only to audit information maintained within the agency information system and does not include audit information maintained by the CSP

b.agency_actions: Determine personnel or roles to be notified in the event of unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of audit information
b.fedramp_guidance: This control part should apply to events detected by the agency AND events detected by the CSP.

_.agency_actions: Restrict access to management of audit logging functionality
_.fedramp_guidance: This control specifically addresses access to management or configuration of logging functionality, not the log data itself. This control applies only to audit information maintained within the agency information system and does not include audit information maintained by the CSP

_.agency_actions: Define audit record retention periods
_.fedramp_guidance: Determine the required audit record retention period considering both statutory and operational requirements. Review the CSP provided log retention services and ensure that any gap is covered by agency controlled log retention.
_.notes: For example, an agency is required by statute to maintain logs of certain system activity for 10 years. The CSP retains logs for 5 years. The agency should implement an automated process to download logs before the 5 year expiration into agency controlled storage where the logs can remain for the additional duration.  Alternatively, the agency may request the CSP extend the duration of log retention. This may result in additional fees and should be explicitly documented in the agency’ contract with the CSP.

a.agency_actions: Review Cloud Service documentation
a.fedramp_guidance: Verify that audit records defined in AU-2 are captured by the CSP. The CSP should provide specific tests to demonstrate compliance. FedRAMP assigns the CSP's own response the broadest scope for this parameter — all system and network components where audit capability is available — as context for what the CSP's package should already cover; it doesn't fix the agency's own determination for any agency-operated components in a hybrid system.

b.fedramp_guidance: Verify that the CSP logging configuration is securely managed. The CSP should provide specific tests to demonstrate compliance.

c.fedramp_guidance: Verify that audit records defined in AU-2 are generated and include the correct information. The CSP should provide specific tests to demonstrate compliance.

a.agency_actions: Document policy and procedure control decisions that are specific to this information system
a.fedramp_guidance: Some policies and procedures will be inherited from other agency systems and/or cloud systems. You do not need to repeat that information here.

b.fedramp_guidance: Determine the agency role or personnel accountable for the policies and procedures in this control family. This is an agency position and should not be assigned to the cloud service provider. This person or role may not be responsible for all implementation, monitoring, or enforcement of the controls but should be accountable to leadership for compliance with all relevant policies and procedures.

c.fedramp_guidance: How often and by whom will the policies and procedures in this control family be reviewed? Provide a broad policy here (e.g. “Policies and procedures will be reviewed at least annually or in response to any relevant incidents or changes”) and then provide more detailed additional review requirements for specific controls as needed.

a.agency_actions: Select an assessor or assessment team for the agency information system
a.fedramp_guidance: The selected assessor or assessment team will be responsible for monitoring the implementation of agency controls. This is a separate activity from the assessment of the cloud service performed by the independent assessor and the FedRAMP team. It is also separate from the continuous monitoring of the CSP performed by the agency. The scope of this assessment should be limited to the controls implemented by the agency. FedRAMP assigns this control's individuals/roles parameter to include FedRAMP and agency customers directly, so the CSP's own control-assessment results already reach the agency as a matter of course rather than needing to be requested separately.

b.agency_actions: Select controls and procedures for the assessment including the frequency with which each control is assessed; create an assessment plan to document these decisions
b.fedramp_guidance: Agencies should adopt automated persistent monitoring of control compliance and effectiveness where possible. Modern attack patterns mean that annual, monthly, and even weekly reviews are probably not sufficient to identify and stop an attack. Agencies should select controls to assess based on risk and resource availability. It may not be practical to monitor all controls equally so a risk based decision process is needed.
b.notes: Many cloud based GRC tools available in the FedRAMP marketplace are designed with automated compliance monitoring built in. Procurement of modern GRC tooling for the agency can significantly reduce workload for internal auditing and make it much simpler to incorporate CSP provided machine readable assessment data.

c.agency_actions: Review the plan with the Authorizing Official or designated representative and address any issues
c.fedramp_guidance: The assessment plan will require risk based decisions balancing risk and resources. The AO must understand the trade offs in the assessment plan and explicitly accept any risks.

d.agency_actions: Assess the system controls as required by the plan
d.fedramp_guidance: Agencies should pursue automated assessment whenever possible to ensure consistency and reduce workloads. Automated assessment results must still be reviewed by the assessor or assessment team.

e.agency_actions: Document the results of the assessment
e.fedramp_guidance: Persistent assessment results can be made available in dashboards or through other automated mechanisms. A formal assessment report may not be required as long as the information is being communicated effectively.

f.agency_actions: Distribute the assessment results as needed.
f.fedramp_guidance: The agency should ensure that results are distributed AND reviewed by required approvers.

_.agency_actions: Use assessors or assessment teams without conflicts or interest
_.fedramp_guidance: Assessors should not share responsibility for system operation or other business needs. The use of automated assessment can significantly reduce this burden by minimizing bias in assessment results.

_.agency_actions: Leverage results from other assessments
_.fedramp_guidance: This control is intended to minimize the assessment burden on the agency. FedRAMP assigns the external organization in this control to mean any FedRAMP Recognized independent assessment service — the same body that already assessed the CSP for certification. Agencies can leverage that assessment for the security objectives it already covers rather than reassessing them independently.

a.agency_actions: Identify and approve each exchange of information between this system and other systems.
a.fedramp_guidance: The relationship with the cloud service provider itself is covered by the FedRAMP Certification Package and the SA-09 External System Service framing, and does not need a separate interconnection agreement. What this control captures is the other end: agency systems and third-party systems that exchange data with the cloud service. Enumerate those exchanges and record the agreement type covering each.

b.agency_actions: Document the interface characteristics, security requirements, and impact level for each exchange.
b.fedramp_guidance: For each exchange record what moves, in which direction, over which interface, and at what impact level. The impact level should be consistent with the categorization assigned under RA-02; an exchange carrying data more sensitive than the receiving system is authorized for is the finding this control exists to surface.

c.agency_actions: Determine the frequency for reviewing and updating exchange agreements.
c.fedramp_guidance: Determine the frequency or triggers that will require an exchange agreement review. Provider change is a natural trigger — CCM-AGM-ROR requires agencies to review each Ongoing Certification Report, and a change to the service's interfaces or information flows should prompt a review of the agreements that depend on them.

a.agency_actions: Assign an Authorizing Official (AO) for the agency information system
a.fedramp_guidance: The AO for the agency information system authorizes the use of the cloud service ONLY within the context of the approved use cases and business processes defined in AC-02 Part a.

b.agency_actions: Assign an Authorizing Official (AO) for common controls available for inheritance by organizational systems
b.fedramp_guidance: In some cases, the agency information system may operate as a pass through providing access to the cloud service offering for other agency information systems. For example, the agency CIOs office may authorize a cloud service that provides vulnerability scanning with the intention that this vulnerability scanning be used in other agency systems. In this case, although the cloud service provider itself is an external system the agency information system can become a common control provider.
b.notes: I know this is confusing. The CIO accepts the risk of using the CSO on behalf of the agency. Other AOs within the agency can then inherit common controls from the CIO authorized system when using the CSO in their own systems. This reduces the overall assessment burden in the agency while maintaining a clear chain of accountability for risk acceptance.

c.agency_actions: Ensure the Authorizing Official understands and accepts all risks associated with the use of the information system for the authorized use case(s)
c.fedramp_guidance: The Authorizing Official's acceptance covers both the controls the agency implements and the risk it inherits from the cloud service. Ensure the AO has seen what the provider does not do as well as what it does: accepted vulnerabilities, any FedRAMP requirements the provider does not meet, and the residual risks recorded elsewhere in this table. AGU-USE-ABU makes completing the ATO process mandatory for federal information systems that use FedRAMP Certified cloud service offerings.

d.agency_actions: Ensure the Authorizing Official for common controls understands and accepts all risks associated with the use of the information system for the authorized use case(s)
d.fedramp_guidance: The cloud service is not a common control provider. Under the SA-09 External System Service framing its risks are accepted by the system's own Authorizing Official rather than by a common control AO. This part applies to the genuine agency common control providers this information system inherits from — the enterprise identity provider, network, and endpoint management systems.

e.agency_actions: Determine the frequency for reviewing and updating authorizations.
e.fedramp_guidance: Determine the frequency or triggers that will require the authorization to be reviewed. Beyond the agency's own cycle, provider events should trigger one: a transformative change, a FedRAMP Reportable Incident, or a change in the service's certification status. CCM-AGM-ROR requires agencies to review each Ongoing Certification Report for exactly this purpose.

a.agency_actions: Determine system level metrics to be monitored
a.fedramp_guidance: System level metrics to be monitored may include metrics from agency implemented controls as well as metrics provided by the CSP.

b.agency_actions: Establish frequency for monitoring and for assessment of control effectiveness
b.fedramp_guidance: Agencies should determine the frequency with which monitored metrics will be reported and include alerts that will trigger if no data is received. Agencies must also identify metrics that indicate the effectiveness of controls, not just compliance.

c.agency_actions: Comply with agency policies for continuous assessment
c.fedramp_guidance: Follow the FedRAMP Continuous Collaborative Monitoring, Significant Change Notification, Vulnerability Detection and Response, and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules. The agency assesses the controls it implements; the provider's controls are assessed through the certification process and its ongoing reporting. Scope the agency's ongoing assessment to the agency-implemented controls identified in CA-02 b rather than re-assessing the service.

d.agency_actions: Comply with agency policies for continuous monitoring
d.fedramp_guidance: Follow the FedRAMP Continuous Collaborative Monitoring, Significant Change Notification, Vulnerability Detection and Response, and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules. Provider-side monitoring reaches the agency through the Ongoing Certification Report supplied every three months under CCM-OCR-AVL and through incident notification; CCM-AGM-ROR makes reviewing each report mandatory. Decide in advance who receives these reports and what happens when one contains something material.

e.agency_actions: Analyze assessment and monitoring results
e.fedramp_guidance: A good test when considering what data needs to be collected is determining how the data will be used. If analysis is not possible because of missing data this must be corrected. Conversely, collecting data that is never used may be an inefficient use of resources.

f.agency_actions: Respond appropriately to assessment and monitoring results
f.fedramp_guidance: Appropriate responses may include any action that addresses or intends to address the results. For example, opening a POA\&M, adjusting automated monitoring, opening an incident, or adjusting alerting thresholds are all valid responses.

g.agency_actions: Report the security and privacy status of the system
g.fedramp_guidance: The agency should ensure that results are distributed AND reviewed by required approvers.

_.agency_actions: Use assessors or assessment teams without conflicts or interest
_.fedramp_guidance: Assessors should not share responsibility for system operation or other business needs. The use of automated assessment can significantly reduce this burden by minimizing bias in assessment results.

_.agency_actions: Ensure risk monitoring is an integral part of the continuous monitoring strategy
_.fedramp_guidance: The risk posture of a system can change due to a wide variety of events. New vulnerabilities disclosed in leveraged software or services, changes in adversary tactics or capabilities, change in the real or perceived value of data, public attention or press related to the agency or agency information system, etc. Continuous risk analysis is critical to ensuring that monitoring strategies provide sufficient risk mitigation to meet agency requirements.

_.agency_actions: Determine penetration testing needs
_.fedramp_guidance: Evaluate penetration testing conducted by the cloud service provider. Rev5 Class C/D packages must document an independent third-party pen test and red-team exercise annually (CA-08 (01)/(02)); Class B only requires pen testing generally (CA-08).  Under 20x, it's absorbed into the continuous vulnerability detection obligation rather than a discrete annual event.

_.agency_actions: Determine penetration testing needs
_.fedramp_guidance: See CA-08 — this enhancement adds the independent-tester requirement at Class C/D.

a.agency_actions: Document configuration management control decisions that are specific to this information system
a.fedramp_guidance: Some policies and procedures will be inherited from other agency systems and/or cloud systems. You do not need to repeat that information here.

b.fedramp_guidance: Determine the agency role or personnel accountable for the policies and procedures in this control family. This is an agency position and should not be assigned to the cloud service provider. This person or role may not be responsible for all implementation, monitoring, or enforcement of the controls but should be accountable to leadership for compliance with all relevant policies and procedures.

Provide a broad policy here (e.g. “Policies and procedures will be reviewed at least annually or in response to any relevant incidents or changes”) and then provide more detailed additional review requirements for specific controls as needed.

a.agency_actions: Document and maintain agency specific configuration settings
a.fedramp_guidance: Maintain accurate and current documentation of any settings, options, configuration, etc. This documentation should be sufficient to recreate the information system from scratch.
a.notes: When possible, maintain this configuration s code. In many cases cloud services can be configured through a user interface or an API. Using an API to apply the desired configuration is generally more reliable and simpler.

b.agency_actions: Review and update documentation when changes are made to the agency controlled settings AND when changes are made by the cloud service provider
b.fedramp_guidance: In addition to updating documentation when the agency changes a setting, it is also important to review documentation in response to updates on the provider side to make sure your current configuration document is still accurate.
b.notes: If you are documenting configuration through a UI, be sure to update the documentation whenever the UI changes.

_.agency_actions: Use automation to maintain and validate configuration documentation
_.fedramp_guidance: When possible, agencies should use modern tools to monitor the applied configuration of the cloud service to detect drift.  Agencies may also want to leverage provider tools that allow you to dump or backup configuration settings as a method of creating documentation.

_.agency_actions: Retain previous versions of baseline configurations
_.fedramp_guidance: As the system configuration changes, create an export of the configuration, and store it in a central repository.

_.agency_actions: Confirm the agency's travel-device policy covers systems/components used to access this cloud service, and define supply-chain handling requirements (e.g., sanitization on receipt, secure/cleared shipping) for any physical infrastructure components being relocated, procured, or disposed of.
_.fedramp_guidance: This is an agency device-management and supply-chain control, not something the CSP's package addresses — the CSP has no traveling infrastructure of its own relevant to the agency's system. Inherit from the agency's existing high-risk-travel device policy for endpoints, and apply the agency's supply-chain risk management requirements (e.g., sanitizing servers on receipt from a vendor, requiring cleared couriers for physical shipment) to any physical components the agency relocates, procures, or disposes of.

a.agency_actions: Identify the kinds of changes that will be implemented by the agency
a.fedramp_guidance: Generally this will be configuration changes and not code deployments.

b.fedramp_guidance: This can be integrated with existing agency configuration management procedures or can be a lighter version based on the use case and risk.

c.fedramp_guidance: The configuration management process must record in a central location all changes made including the reason for the change. The process should also ensure baseline documentation is updated and all required parties are notified.

d.agency_actions: Implement approved changes
d.fedramp_guidance: Only approved changes may be implemented. Agencies should consider the risk associated with different kinds of changes and tailor the configuration management process. For example, changes in sensitive configuration settings should be reviewed closely before being implemented, but adding or removing a user may not require as much scrutiny.

e.agency_actions: Retain records of changes
e.fedramp_guidance: Records of changes are important for troubleshooting and are also critical if the information system needs to be re-built. At a minimum records of changes need to be maintained until all baseline documentation has been updated to reflect the change.

f.agency_actions: Monitor configuration controlled settings for drift
f.fedramp_guidance: If configuration settings can be accessed via an API or CLI it is recommended to maintain all configuration settings as code under version control. This makes it trivial to confirm that current settings match the expected configuration and to revert to the approved configuration if unauthorized changes are found.

g.agency_actions: Maintain a change management process appropriate for the risk associated with the system
g.fedramp_guidance: Consider carefully the change management process for the information system. Systems that handle low risk data and are managed by small teams will not require as complex and rigid a configuration management process as systems that handle sensitive data or are administered by a large team.

_.agency_actions: Test, validate, and document changes
_.fedramp_guidance: Ensure that your change management process includes steps that test the change before deployment when feasible, validate the change was successfully deployed, and verify documentation was updated.

_.agency_actions: Ensure security and privacy representatives are included in the change management process
_.fedramp_guidance: Change management needs to include engineering and system administration teams who actually design and deploy changes as well as security and privacy officers.

_.agency_actions: Conduct impact analysis of all system changes
_.fedramp_guidance: The agency should conduct an analysis of all system changes including changes to the cloud service performed by the provider to determine the impact to security and privacy. Provider changes must be reviewed to determine if the risk posture of the system still meets the agency's needs.

_.agency_actions: Verify security controls after system changes
_.fedramp_guidance: Agencies should review the security status of impacted controls after system changes to verify that all security controls are still functioning as expected.

_.agency_actions: Define, document, approve, and enforce logical access restrictions associated with changes to the system.
_.fedramp_guidance: In most cases, physical access to cloud service applications will be handled by the provider or their IaaS/PaaS provider. Agencies should still document and enforce logical access restrictions for system changes managed by agency administrators when appropriate. Consult the provider's secure configuration guidance for information.

_.agency_actions: Automatically enforce and log enforcement of logical access controls
_.fedramp_guidance: Enforcement of access restrictions on changes to the cloud service is implemented by the CSP. The agency's part is confirming that the record of enforcement — who attempted a change, what was blocked, and what was allowed — is available to the agency and not only to the provider. Review the Secure Configuration Guide for the administrative event feeds the service exposes and route them to agency monitoring. No Key Security Indicator maps to this enhancement, so a 20x package will not contain a directly corresponding entry.

a.agency_actions: Limit privileges in production or operational environment
a.fedramp_guidance: Consult the provider to determine if a testing or staging instance of the cloud service offering is available. Consider implementing a CI/CD pipeline to manage how changes are deployed to the production environment.

b.fedramp_guidance: Determine how often privileges for individuals and service accounts should be reviewed. This overlaps with AC-06's privilege-review cadence — reference that entry for the mechanics rather than repeating it here.

a.agency_actions: Ensure configuration settings comply with least privilege principles
a.fedramp_guidance: All configuration settings should be selected to reflect the most restrictive mode consistent with operational requirements

b.fedramp_guidance: If configuration settings can be accessed via an API or CLI it is recommended to maintain all configuration settings as code under version control. This makes it trivial to confirm that current settings match the expected configuration and to revert to the approved configuration if unauthorized changes are found.

c.agency_actions: Identify, document, and approve any deviations from established configuration settings
c.fedramp_guidance: If a setting is temporarily changed in response to a critical issue (e.g., business need, security incident, testing, etc.) the reason for the change should be clearly documented and approved by the Authorizing Official or their delegate.

d.agency_actions: Monitor configuration controlled settings for drift
d.fedramp_guidance: If configuration settings can be accessed via an API or CLI it is recommended to maintain all configuration settings as code under version control. _.fedramp_guidance: In critical systems, use CI/CD or similar tools to manage configuration settings automatically.

a.fedramp_guidance: Review the CSP's Secure Configuration Guide (SCG-CSO-RSC) for the specific functions it exposes as configurable, and disable those not required for the agency's use case.

b.agency_actions: Prohibit or restrict the use of high risk functions that are not required to achieve mission goals.
b.fedramp_guidance: Review the CSP's Secure Configuration Guide (SCG-CSO-RSC) for the specific high-risk functions, ports, protocols, and services it exposes as configurable, and restrict those not required for the agency's use case.

b.fedramp_guidance: Where the service is licensed per named user or per seat, the account inventory maintained under AC-02 is also the licence inventory — keep one source rather than two. Reconcile assigned seats against active accounts on the same cycle as the account review defined in AC-02 j.

Review the Secure Configuration Guide for public link sharing, guest access, and external collaboration settings, and restrict the ones the authorized use cases do not require; AGU-USE-RSG requires agencies to review provider Secure Configuration Guides and configure relevant security settings.

c.fedramp_guidance: Coordinate contingency planning activities with incident handling activities by establishing clear roles and responsibilities for each phase of an event, defining activation criteria for contingency operations, integrating incident response and contingency plans, maintaining shared situational awareness, conducting joint exercises with the cloud provider, and continuously improving both plans through lessons learned.

e.agency_actions: Review updates to the contingency plan

f.fedramp_guidance: Communicate contingency plan changes to ensure all impacted agency stakeholders understand what changed, why it changed, when it becomes effective, and what actions they need to take.

a.agency_actions: Develop security and privacy plans for the system
a.fedramp_guidance: Agency security and privacy plans should be scoped to the controls for which the agency has implementation responsibility. Controls that are fully implemented by the provider may be excluded from the plans, or included with an attestation that the control is implemented by the provider. It is not required that the plan include details of the provider’s implementation unless the agency feels it provides additional value to users of the system.

b.agency_actions: Distribute copies of the plans and communicate subsequent changes to the plans
b.fedramp_guidance: Distribute the plans to the agency roles accountable for implementing and assessing them and to the Authorizing Official. Because much of this system's risk is inherited from the cloud service, include whoever tracks provider reporting under CCM-AGM-ROR — they are the ones who will notice when a provider change makes the plan inaccurate.

c.fedramp_guidance: Determine the frequency or triggers that will require the plans to be reviewed. Provider change is the trigger most likely to be missed: a transformative change to the cloud service can invalidate the plan's description of the operational environment and its dependencies well before the agency's own review cycle comes round.

d.agency_actions: Update the plans as needed
d.fedramp_guidance: The parts of the plan most likely to go stale for a system of this kind are the component inventory, the description of connections and dependencies, and the set of authorized use cases recorded under AC-02 a. Update those first.

e.agency_actions: Protect the plans from unauthorized disclosure and modification
e.fedramp_guidance: The plans describe where the system's weaknesses are, so treat them as sensitive. Keep them under version control with access limited to the roles that need it, and record who approved each revision. Where the agency holds the provider's Certification Package alongside its own plans, apply the same handling to both.

a.agency_actions: Develop Rules of behavior for organizational users
a.fedramp_guidance: RoB should clearly describe the system usage, security, and privacy expectations for users of the system. In some cases existing RoB may be sufficient.

b.agency_actions: Capture user agreement to the Rules of Behavior
b.fedramp_guidance: This is normally inherited from the agency's existing acknowledgement process; the requirement is that it happens before access to this system is granted. Where the cloud service can gate first login on an acceptance step, use it; otherwise tie acknowledgement to the access approval process defined in AC-02 e.

c.agency_actions: Periodically review and update the Rules of Behavior
c.fedramp_guidance: Determine the frequency or triggers that will require the rules of behavior to be reviewed. New capabilities in the cloud service — external sharing, generative AI features, mobile clients — are a common trigger, because they create behaviours the existing rules did not anticipate.

d.agency_actions: Require individuals who have acknowledged a previous version of the rules of behavior to read and re-acknowledge when the rules are updated
d.fedramp_guidance: Re-acknowledgement is normally handled by the same agency system that captures the original acknowledgement. Confirm that a revision triggers it rather than relying on the annual cycle to catch up.

_.agency_actions: Include in the rules of behavior, restrictions on: (a) Use of social media, social networking sites, and external sites/applications; (b) Posting organizational information on public websites; and (c) Use of organization-provided identifiers (e.g., email addresses) and authentication secrets (e.g., passwords) for creating accounts on external sites/applications.
_.fedramp_guidance: Two points matter most for a system built on a cloud service: agency identifiers and authentication secrets should not be used to create accounts on external sites, and agency information should not be moved into external services that have not been authorized. Where the cloud service offers integrations with external applications, review the Secure Configuration Guide and restrict which ones users can enable for themselves.

This part therefore applies to the other external personnel the agency brings to the system, such as integrators and managed service staff.

b.agency_actions: Require external providers to comply with agency personnel security policies.
b.fedramp_guidance: Place this obligation in the contract with the integrator or support vendor. It does not extend to the cloud service provider, whose personnel security obligations are set by FedRAMP.

c.fedramp_guidance: FedRAMP guidance for PS-07 requires providers to clearly document any nationality requirements for every account type in the platform, and to state explicitly when none exists. e.fedramp_guidance: Provider compliance reaches the agency through ongoing certification reporting rather than direct oversight; CCM-AGM-ROR requires agencies to review each Ongoing Certification Report.

b.fedramp_guidance: Determine who must be notified and within what period. Where the individual holds privileged access to this system, include the Access Control Officer designated under AC-02 b so that access can be reviewed in parallel.

a.agency_actions: Categorize the Information System and associated information
a.fedramp_guidance: Categorize the information system according to the type of information it processes, stores, or transmits, and assess the potential impact if compromised. Use the actual use case rather than the default Cloud Systems categorization.  Categorization should capture not just the technical setup of the cloud provider, but also how the agency truly uses the product, the nature of the data entrusted to it, the potential mission consequences if something goes wrong, and all relevant privacy, records, legal, and security obligations.

b.fedramp_guidance: Document the results of security categorization and the reasoning behind them in the system’s security plan, explaining why they matter. Conduct Privacy Threshold Analysis (PTA) to determine if the system will collect  personal data. If it does, conduct a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA). Follow FIPS 199 and NIST SP 800-60.

c.agency_actions: Ensure the authorizing official or designated representative reviews and approves the security categorization decision
c.fedramp_guidance: The categorization drives everything downstream — the FedRAMP class the agency should require of the service, the controls in scope, and the risk the Authorizing Official is accepting. Record the AO's approval against the categorization rationale documented under RA-02 b rather than against the impact level alone.

a.agency_actions: Conduct a risk assessment for the agency information system.
a.fedramp_guidance: The provider's vulnerabilities and their evaluation reach the agency through the FedRAMP Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules; the agency does not repeat that analysis. What the agency assesses is what those provider-side facts mean for its own mission, together with the risks arising from how the agency configures and uses the service. VER-EVA-EPA requires providers to estimate the potential agency impact of exploitation — treat that estimate as an input, not as the agency's conclusion.

b.agency_actions: Integrate system-level risk assessment results with agency and mission risk management.
b.fedramp_guidance: Where the same cloud service supports several agency systems, a vulnerability or outage in it is a shared risk rather than a system-specific one. Ensure the agency risk function sees the aggregate rather than each system's view in isolation.

c.fedramp_guidance: Record these in the agency SSP or a separate risk assessment report, whichever the agency uses. Include the risks the agency has accepted because they cannot be remediated by configuration — this table identifies several of them.

d.agency_actions: Determine the frequency for reviewing risk assessment results.
d.fedramp_guidance: Determine the frequency or triggers that will require a review. Provider reporting supplies a natural cadence: vulnerability activity is reported at least monthly under VER-TFR-MHR, and the Ongoing Certification Report arrives every three months under CCM-OCR-AVL.

e.agency_actions: Identify who receives risk assessment results.
e.fedramp_guidance: Include the Authorizing Official and the roles accountable for the control families in this table. VER-AGM-RVR expects agencies to review provider vulnerability reports at intervals commensurate with the risk posture in their ATO, so whoever performs that review needs these results as context.

f.agency_actions: Determine the frequency and triggers for updating the risk assessment.
f.fedramp_guidance: A transformative change to the cloud service is the trigger most specific to this system. Significant change notifications and the Ongoing Certification Report are how the agency learns of them.
